parameters.text: A prompt goes out over a streamed POST; tokens come back one at a time. The transcript lives in the global store named "chat", so every page here sees it.

The dispatcher executes exactly two things: a built-in you enabled by name, and an action type an Action Handler in this graph registered. Everything else is refused, with a reason, on the outputs below.
Pulling structure out of a streamed answer
Pattern Extractor reads the finished answer from the same global store the Chat page writes. Send a prompt there first, then extract here.
State History watches one key of the "chat" store. An undo is an ordinary store commit, so everything subscribed to that key sees it.
Saving a checkpoint does not touch the undo stack. Restoring one is an ordinary write, so it is itself undoable.
Apply shows the new title immediately. Commit keeps it; Rollback puts the old one back — unless something else wrote the key first, in which case the newer value stands and the reason says so.
WebSocket when the client needs to talk back mid-stream. Reconnection, the send queue and the close code are all outputs, so an outage is visible rather than looking like a slow server.
Stream Buffer collects messages and releases them in batches, so a burst repaints once instead of once per message.
A server that batches JSON objects into one frame, or splits one across frames, does not hand you message boundaries. The parser scans incrementally and only emits complete values.
